title: About
text: I am an applied mathematician at INSA Toulouse, where I develop fast and reliable reduced-order models for flows governed by partial differential equations, with a particular focus on flood simulation.

title: About
text:
My path
I studied mathematical engineering at Sultan Moulay Slimane University in Morocco, then moved to France for a master’s degree in applied mathematics at the Université de Pau et des Pays de l’Adour, specializing in modeling and numerical simulation. My master’s internship at INSA Toulouse, on physics-informed machine learning for reduced-order models, set the direction of my research.
I then did my PhD at INSA Toulouse, within the Institut de Mathématiques de Toulouse, on reduced-order models for the two-dimensional shallow-water equations, applied to real flood events. Since 2024, I have been a Teaching and Research Associate (ATER) at INSA Toulouse, where I continue this research and teach mathematics and numerical methods to engineering students.

title: Research
text: Many problems in science and engineering are described by partial differential equations (PDEs). Solving them accurately with high-fidelity numerical methods is often very costly, which becomes prohibitive when the same model must be run many times: for forecasting, optimization, control or uncertainty quantification (UQ). My research develops reduced-order models (ROMs) and surrogate models that make these computations fast while preserving accuracy and the underlying physics.

title: Research
text:
ROMs in a nutshell
The solutions of a PDE often live, in practice, close to a space of much lower dimension than the full numerical model. A ROM exploits this: it learns a small set of representative modes from high-fidelity solutions, then describes any new solution with only a few coefficients.
The computational effort is split into two stages:

Offline, done once: high-fidelity simulations are computed and compressed into a reduced basis, for instance by Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD).
Online, done many times: for a new parameter or scenario, only the few reduced coefficients are computed, which is orders of magnitude cheaper.







flowchart LR
  A["Full-order model<br/>(PDE solver)"] --> B["Snapshots of<br/>the solution"]
  B --> C["Reduced basis<br/>(e.g. POD)"]
  C --> D["Intrusive:<br/>projection of the equations"]
  C --> E["Non-intrusive:<br/>learning from data"]
  D --> F["Fast online<br/>predictions"]
  E --> F







General principle of a ROM: a reduced basis is extracted offline, then the reduced dynamics are obtained either by projecting the equations (intrusive) or by learning them from data (non-intrusive).

title: Research
text:
Two families of approaches


 Intrusive ROMs
The governing equations are projected onto the reduced basis (Galerkin-type methods). This requires access to the operators of the numerical solver, but keeps a direct link with the physics and allows error control.
Application: advection–diffusion problems.


 Non-intrusive ROMs
The reduced dynamics are learned directly from simulation data, for instance with neural networks, without modifying the solver. This makes the approach usable with existing, complex or industrial codes.
Application: 2D shallow-water equations and flood simulation.

title: Research
text:
Application to floods
The two-dimensional shallow-water equations (SWE), also known as the Saint-Venant equations, describe free-surface flows in rivers and floodplains. They are central to flood forecasting, but their high-fidelity simulation is costly, and the solutions are hard to reduce: the dynamics are nonlinear and the wet/dry fronts move as the flood spreads.
My work builds non-intrusive ROMs for the 2D SWE that remain accurate on flood scenarios not seen during training, follow moving flood fronts, and respect physical quantities such as mass.

title: Research
text:
Main contributions
My work has addressed several difficulties that make floods hard to reduce:

Accuracy with few modes. By learning the POD projection error together with the reduced coefficients, the reduced model stays accurate with a small basis and compact neural networks, and was validated on real floods of the Aude river and the city of Abidjan.
Moving flood fronts. Registering the moving wetted area onto a fixed domain, combined with a global water-volume constraint, captures advancing fronts with far fewer modes and much smaller errors.
Changing flow regimes. Local ROMs, each adapted to a flow regime and selected online by a physics-guided classifier, improve accuracy when a single global model is not enough.
Speed for many-query studies. The resulting surrogates simulate whole flood events in seconds, making large ensembles and uncertainty quantification affordable.

See all publications

title: Research
text:
Projects & collaborations
My PhD and my position as Teaching and Research Associate (2021–2026) were carried out at the Institut de Mathématiques de Toulouse (IMT), INSA Toulouse. During my PhD, I contributed to the ANR MUFFINS project, in collaboration with INRAE, on efficient simulation and model reduction for hydrodynamic applications.
I have worked with Jérôme Monnier (INSA Toulouse, IMT), Robin Bouclier (INSA Toulouse, Institut Clément Ader) and Pierre-André Garambois (INRAE, Aix-en-Provence).

title: Research
text:
Looking ahead
I want to extend physics-guided, non-intrusive model reduction to broader computational fluid dynamics. Directions I am particularly interested in:

Structure-preserving ROMs: reduced models that retain the key properties of the original equations, such as conservation laws, stability or energy balance.
Parametric and unsteady flows, with ROMs valid over wide ranges of physical parameters.
UQ, where fast surrogates make large ensembles of simulations affordable.
Coupling numerical solvers with learned surrogates, to combine the reliability of physics-based models with the speed of machine learning.

The common thread is ROMs that are fast, interpretable and reliable across flow regimes.
Beyond hydrodynamics, I am open to applying ROMs to other fields where high-fidelity simulations are a bottleneck, such as weather and climate modeling, ocean and atmospheric flows, environmental engineering, energy systems, or industrial fluid mechanics, and I welcome collaborations in these areas.

title: Publications
text:
Journal articles

Published · 2024

Reduction of the shallow water system by an error aware POD-neural network method: Application to floodplain dynamics
M. Allabou, R. Bouclier, P.-A. Garambois and J. Monnier
Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering, 428, 117094, 2024.

A non-intrusive reduced model for 2D flood simulation: POD extracts a few dominant flow patterns, and neural networks learn how they evolve, without opening the simulation code. By accounting for the projection error, the method stays accurate with few modes and small networks, even for convection-dominated flows. Applied to the flooding of the Aude river (southern France), it reproduces water levels and discharges of the full 2D model and opens the way to real-time simulation of large floodplains.

title: Publications
text:
Submitted manuscripts

Submitted · 2026

Registering wetting fronts by dilation: a non-intrusive shallow-water reduced-order model with global mass closure for flood forecasting
M. Allabou
Submitted to Advances in Computational Mathematics.

Moving flood fronts are hard to capture with a fixed reduced basis. This work maps the moving wetted area onto a fixed reference domain before compression, and recovers the front position from the conservation of the total water volume. The flow is then described with three to four times fewer modes, and water-depth errors are 12 to 20 times lower than with standard POD–NN. An ensemble of 10,000 flood events runs in about three minutes on a laptop, making probabilistic flood forecasting affordable.

In preparation · 2026

Toward fast flood simulations via reduced-order 2D shallow water modeling
M. Allabou, L. Pujol, R. Bouclier, P.-A. Garambois and J. Monnier

A reduced model of urban flooding, trained on high-fidelity 2D shallow-water simulations over the city of Abidjan and tested on the real 2018 flood event. It reproduces water depths and velocities over the whole event with centimetre-level errors, and simulates the 8.3-hour flood in about 11 seconds, roughly 420 times faster than the full model, a step toward real-time flood forecasting and digital twins.

Related research



In preparation · 2026

Physics-guided regime-adaptive reduced-order modelling for shallow-water flows and flood uncertainty quantification
M. Allabou

Instead of a single global model, this framework uses several local reduced models, each adapted to a flow regime (wetting fronts, hydraulic jumps, overbank flow), and a physics-guided classifier that selects the right one during the simulation. On a 2D flood benchmark with 400 scenarios, it halves the error of a global ROM, and it shows that reliable ROMs for nonlinear flows depend as much on choosing the right local model as on the model itself.

title: Publications
text:
PhD thesis

Defended · March 2026

Reduced-order modeling of the two-dimensional shallow-water equations using an error-aware POD–neural-network method: application to flood dynamics
M. Allabou
PhD in Applied Mathematics, INSA Toulouse – Institut de Mathématiques de Toulouse, 2026.

A non-intrusive reduced model for 2D shallow-water flows, built from POD and neural networks, with a key ingredient: learning the projection error, which keeps the model accurate with few modes and compact networks. The thesis also reduces the input signals (upstream hydrographs) with BiLSTM autoencoders, forming a complete reduction chain from inputs to outputs. Tested on two real 2018 floods, the Aude river (France) and the city of Abidjan (Côte d’Ivoire), the surrogate predicts floods on large meshes in a few seconds, and points to overflow-dominated urban flows as the next challenge.
